exposure: maternal age at first birth (advanced maternal age, 35+ years, 40+ years vs 20-34 years)
cohort: The study included 6831 first-time mothers with singleton births in Vienna, Austria, between 2010 and 2019.
finding: Advanced maternal age at first birth is significantly associated with a higher risk of preterm births, medically induced labor, cesarean sections, and low-weight newborns, but not Apgar scores.
mod_finding: Advanced maternal age at first birth is significantly associated with an increased rate of medically induced labor and cesarean sections.
birth_weight: singleton newborns, with a specific focus on low-weight newborns (< 2500 g)
gest_age: singleton newborns, with a specific focus on preterm birth (< 37th gestational week)
